response.sql: WITH fc AS (SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(fa.actor_id) AS n FROM film f LEFT JOIN film_actor fa ON fa.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg1 FROM fc), s1 AS (SELECT fc.film_id, fc.n, fc.n - a1.avg1 AS ex1 FROM fc CROSS JOIN a1 WHERE fc.n > a1.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.film_id, s1.n, s1.ex1, s1.n - a2.avg2 AS ex2 FROM s1 CROSS JOIN a2 WHERE s1.n > a2.avg2) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actor_count, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_avg, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second_avg FROM s2

assumptions.assumption: 'Each film' means every row in film, so films with no film_actor rows count as having 0 actors and are included in the first average. If either average is NULL, no films are kept and the query returns one row with NULL values.

alternatives.interpretation: Only films that have at least one film_actor row are counted, so films with zero actors are excluded from the first average.
alternatives.sql: WITH fc AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(actor_id) AS n FROM film_actor GROUP BY film_id), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg1 FROM fc), s1 AS (SELECT fc.film_id, fc.n, fc.n - a1.avg1 AS ex1 FROM fc CROSS JOIN a1 WHERE fc.n > a1.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.film_id, s1.n, s1.ex1, s1.n - a2.avg2 AS ex2 FROM s1 CROSS JOIN a2 WHERE s1.n > a2.avg2) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actor_count, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_avg, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second_avg FROM s2
